first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the current completion decline and has prior evidence of improving time-to-value and adoption. I would verify that evidence and compare it with promotional pricing evidence, especially for qualified-revenue durability, retention, and discount-related risks before committing the sole experiment slot.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified prior test directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and produced +13% completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its +18% qualified-revenue lift came with 12% lower retention and failure by first renewal, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Uncertainty remains about whether the earlier onboarding effect will fully replicate in the current cohort, so retain an experimental holdout rather than broadly rolling out.
